  1. 1 Must see within District 1

    Saigon Notre-Dame Basilica

    The twin-spired red-brick French cathedral (1863-1880) built with imported Marseille materials, on the square opposite the Post Office. UNDER RESTORATION since 2017 (interior closed to visitors; completion pushed to ~2027, scaffolding coming off by early 2026) — view the exterior.

    Look for Colonial cathedral (restoration)

    01 Cong xa Paris, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam

    Recommended by , ,

  2. 2 Must see within District 1 · Cafés

    Ca Phe Do Phu

    The 'Commando Cafe' - a 1940s house that was a secret Viet Cong special-forces base with a weapons bunker and hidden mailbox; today it pours nostalgic bac xiu and serves com tam Dai Han above its wartime tunnel.

    113A Dang Dung, Tan Dinh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam

    Recommended by , ,

  3. 3 Must see within District 1 · Chinese

    Sủi Cảo Hà Tôn Quyền (Thiên Thiên)

    The heart of Saigon's nicknamed 'phố sủi cảo' — a cluster of Hoa family dumpling shops (Thiên Thiên among the best-known) that have run for 30+ years each. Plump shrimp-and-pork sủi cảo steamed, fried, or in clear soup with handmade noodles.

    Hà Tôn Quyền, Ward 4, District 11, Cholon, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam

    Recommended by , ,

  4. 4 Must see within District 1

    Reunification Palace (Independence Palace)

    The modernist 1960s presidential palace where NVA Tank 843 crashed the gate on 30 April 1975, ending the war. Frozen-in-time state rooms, war-command bunker and telecoms basement. National monument; daily ~07:00-18:00, 80,000d.

    Look for Historic palace & war site

    135 Nam Ky Khoi Nghia, Ben Thanh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam

    Recommended by ,

  5. 5 Must see within District 1

    Saigon Central Post Office

    Working 1886-1891 post office (architect Alfred Foulhoux; often mis-credited to Eiffel) with a vaulted iron-truss hall, painted maps and a portrait of Ho Chi Minh. Ranked among the world's most beautiful post offices; still operational.

    Look for Colonial landmark

    125 Cong xa Paris (Hai Ba Trung), Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam

    Recommended by ,

  6. 6 Must see within District 1

    Jade Emperor Pagoda (Phuoc Hai Tu)

    Saigon's most atmospheric Taoist temple, built by the Cantonese community in 1909, thick with incense smoke and carved wooden deities incl. the Hall of Ten Hells and a turtle pond. Obama visited in 2016. Free, ~07:00-18:00.

    Look for Taoist temple

    73 Mai Thi Luu, Da Kao Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam

    Recommended by ,

  7. 7 Must see within District 1

    Nguyen Hue Walking Street & People's Committee Building

    The city's 900 m pedestrian boulevard (a former canal, walkerised 2015) running from the floodlit French Hotel de Ville / People's Committee Building (1898-1909, viewed from outside) and Ho Chi Minh statue down to the Saigon River. Liveliest at night.

    Look for Pedestrian boulevard & civic landmark

    Nguyen Hue Boulevard, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam

    Recommended by ,

  8. 8 Must see within District 1

    Mariamman Hindu Temple (Chua Ba Mariamman)

    Saigon's only Hindu temple, a vivid South-Indian shrine built by Tamil merchants in the late 1800s to the goddess Mariamman, its ~12 m gopuram crowded with painted deities. Free; daily ~07:00-19:00, remove shoes.

    Look for Hindu temple

    45 Truong Dinh, Ben Thanh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam

    Recommended by ,

  9. 9 Must see within District 1

    Bach Dang Wharf & Saigon Waterbus

    The 1.3 km riverside park and pier on the Saigon River where locals gather at sunset and river cruises and the 15,000d public waterbus depart for Thu Duc. The best way to see the city from the water, past Landmark 81 and Bitexco.

    Look for River

    10B Ton Duc Thang, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam

    Recommended by ,

  10. 10 Must see within District 1

    Cầu Ba Son (Thu Thiem 2 Bridge)

    The city's newest icon — a cable-stayed bridge with a single soaring pylon, opened April 2022, linking central District 1 (Mê Linh Square) to the Thủ Thiêm new-urban area. Its artistic night lighting and the riverside park beneath it have made it one of Saigon's most popular sunset and check-in spots on the water.

    Look for Bridge / landmark

    Nối Quận 1 với TP. Thủ Đức (sông Sài Gòn), Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam

    Recommended by ,

  11. 11 Must see within District 1

    Tuyến Metro số 1 Bến Thành - Suối Tiên (Metro Line 1)

    The city's first metro, opened 22 December 2024 after more than a decade of building — and an instant 'triệu-like' check-in phenomenon in its own right. The Bến Thành underground hall's lotus-shaped skylight and the elevated An Phú and Thảo Điền stations (sunset views over Thủ Đức) are the most-photographed spots; ride it as an attraction, not just transport.

    Look for Metro / check-in

    Tuyến Bến Thành (Quận 1) – Suối Tiên (TP. Thủ Đức), Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam

    Recommended by ,

  12. 12 Must see within District 1 · Vietnamese

    Pho Tau Bay

    North-to-South phở institution since 1954, famed for its giant 'to xe lua' (train-car) bowl of simple, garnish-free Northern phở bac that Saigonese have loved for 70+ years.

    435 Ly Thai To, Ward 9, District 10, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam

    Recommended by ,

  13. 13 Must see within District 1 · Chendol

    Che Thai Y Phuong

    The standout of District 10's neon-lit chè Thái street; a famously rich Thai-style sweet soup of pureed durian, jackfruit, palm seed and longan in coconut milk.

    380 Nguyen Tri Phuong, Ward 6, District 10, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam

    Recommended by ,

  14. 14 Must see within District 1 · Vietnamese

    Bun Bo Hue Dong Ba

    A perennially packed bún bò Huế spot beside the Conservatory of Music, singled out by a visiting New York chef as one of the best bowls of soup in all of Vietnam.

    207B Nguyen Van Thu, Da Kao Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam

    Recommended by ,

  15. 15 Must see within District 1 · Cafés

    The Cafe Apartment

    1960s apartment block on the Nguyen Hue walking street turned vertical warren of 50+ cafes; a Saigon coffee landmark.

    42 Nguyen Hue, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam

    Recommended by ,

  16. 16 Must see within District 1 · Vietnamese

    Cuc Gach Quan

    Beloved home-cooking restaurant in restored villas; MICHELIN Bib Gourmand, rice cooked in cast iron on wood stoves.

    10 Dang Tat, Tan Dinh Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam

    Recommended by ,

  17. 17 Must see within District 1 · Vietnamese

    The Lunch Lady

    Nguyen Thi Thanh's canalside stall made famous by Bourdain's No Reservations; a different regional noodle soup each day.

    23 Hoang Sa, Da Kao Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam

    Recommended by ,

  18. 18 Must see within District 1 · Khmer

    Hồ Thị Kỷ Food Street

    A 300m alley market settled by Vietnamese-Cambodian refugees in the 1970s, now Saigon's densest Cambodian-Vietnamese food alley (100+ stalls); Khmer fish noodles, prahok and palm-sugar chè, from ~3pm.

    Hồ Thị Kỷ, Ward 1, District 10, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam

    Recommended by ,

  19. 19 Must see within District 1 · Cafés

    2 Lam Son

    Park Hyatt Saigon's martini bar and one of the city's cocktail landmarks, running guest shifts with bartenders drawn from the World's Best Bars.

    2 Lam Son Square (Park Hyatt Saigon), Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam

    Recommended by ,

  20. 20 Must see within District 1 · Hawker

    Saigon Saigon Bar

    Historic 10th-floor rooftop bar atop the Caravelle Hotel, a wartime haunt of diplomats and correspondents since 1959, with live music and skyline views.

    Caravelle Saigon, 19-23 Lam Son Square, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam

    Recommended by ,

  21. 21 Must see within District 1 · Chinese

    Long Trieu (The Royal Pavilion)

    One MICHELIN Star; chef Angus Chan's refined Cantonese kitchen inside The Reverie, weaving Vietnamese ingredients into Hong Kong technique amid jade and gold-leaf interiors.

    4F, The Reverie Saigon, 22-36 Nguyen Hue, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam

    Recommended by ,

  22. 22 Must see within District 1 · Cafés

    Stir - Modern Classic Cocktail

    Saigon's highest-placed bar on Asia's 50 Best Bars (ranked 2022-2025, No. 61 in 2025) — a speakeasy-jazz room of precise modern-classic drinks.

    1st floor, 136 Lê Thánh Tôn, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam

    Recommended by ,

  23. 23 Must see within District 1 · Vietnamese

    Banh Mi Huynh Hoa

    Saigon's most famous banh mi since 1989 — permanent queues for the thap cam loaded with pate and cold cuts.

    26 Le Thi Rieng Street, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam

    Recommended by ,

  24. 24 Must see within District 1 · Vietnamese

    Anan Saigon

    Chef Peter Cuong Franklin's MICHELIN-starred restaurant over the Ton That Dam market; street food reimagined as fine dining.

    89 Ton That Dam, Ben Nghe Ward, District 1, Ho Chi Minh City, Vietnam

    Recommended by

How we choose

Every place is recommended by named sources (review-aggregator star ratings never count as the recommender), pinned to its door from a published coordinate, and status-checked. Closed places stay, flagged, so you know they’re gone.

Must see
The places to plan a visit around — graded within each area, not across the city.
Worth the detour
Strong picks, worth going out of your way for.
Deep cut
For the curious: smaller, odder, more local.

Within each area, places are ordered by tier, then by number of named sources — never by popularity. No ratings, prices or opening hours are shown, because the guide doesn’t hold verified ones.

105 sights and 66 places to eat in the city of Ho Chi Minh City, each traceable to the source that named it (Michelin, local news & vetted local/viral creators) across 17 districts. Renders in soft pastel, light or dark.

How this guide was made

Web-searched & fact-checked

Every place is traceable to a credible source — Michelin, UNESCO, local news & magazines, and vetted local/viral creators — in data/sources.json. Coordinates are verified into data/geocodes.json and every place status-checked open. Yelp/TripAdvisor never count toward the two-source bar.
